brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 1 November; new research covers 17:10 CET on 31 October to 05:10 CET on 1 November, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Drones Reportedly Hit Lukoil's NORSI Plant in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod Region
items.lede: Footage on Telegram channels showed fires at Russia's fourth-largest refinery about 800 kilometers from Ukraine, though no official confirmed a strike.

sections.text: Lukoil's NORSI oil refinery in Kstovo, in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, was reportedly hit by drones overnight into Sunday, the Kyiv Independent reported [1]. Ukrainian monitoring channels Exilenova+ and Supernova+ posted footage of the alleged attack [1]. Independent Russian outlet ASTRA reported that the refinery was struck and burning [1]. The Kyiv Independent said it could not verify the reports [1]. NORSI is Russia's fourth-largest refinery and processes about 15 million to 17 million metric tons of crude a year, the outlet said [1]. It sits about 800 kilometers (500 miles) from Ukraine's border [1]. No Russian official or Ukrainian military statement was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low, because the strike rests on Telegram channels and ASTRA, relayed by one outlet that could not verify them.

items.title: US Embassy Warns of Credible Mass-Casualty Threat at a Moscow Museum Park
items.lede: Russia's FSB said it acted on the US tip, and the Tsaritsyno grounds were evacuated mid-concert; no attack had been reported by early Sunday.

sections.text: The US Embassy in Russia said on Saturday it was aware of a credible threat of a mass-casualty event that day at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow [2][3]. It said the US government was coordinating a response with Russian authorities and told people to avoid the area [3][4]. Russia's FSB security service told state media it had received information from US partners about a planned terrorist attack and was taking action [3][4]. The park was evacuated during a concert and closed, the Moscow Times reported, citing the outlet Ostorozhno, Novosti! [3]. The embassy did not say who was behind the plot [4]. No attack or casualties were reported in the sources read by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the warning was issued and the FSB acknowledged it, because the embassy text and FSB statement are quoted by three outlets. The evacuation detail rests on a Russian outlet relayed by the Moscow Times.

items.title: Zelensky Says Three-Way Talks With Russia and the US Could Start November 6
items.lede: Kyiv backs the US plan for technical-level talks in Abu Dhabi, though Moscow says the preparations do not commit it to limiting the fighting.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday that preparing for three-way talks on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi does not commit Russia to limit fighting. He said Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries do not affect those talks [5]. The Kyiv Independent, citing an unnamed senior Ukrainian official, reported that Kyiv suspects Moscow of offering a phone call to avoid an in-person leaders' meeting [6]. Late Friday, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told a news conference in Atlanta that if Zelensky wants to meet Putin, he can come to Moscow [7]. Asked by Deutsche Welle about the Kyiv Independent report, Lavrov rejected the idea that the Kremlin wants a phone call rather than an in-person meeting [8][9]. Late Saturday, Zelensky told US interviewer Tony Perkins that the three-way meeting could take place between November 6 and 10 [10]. He said Abu Dhabi was the tentative venue, but neither the dates nor the place were final [10]. He said Ukraine backs the US proposal for technical-level talks [10].

Confidence is high on Peskov's, Lavrov's, and Zelensky's statements, which Interfax, the Kyiv Independent, DW, and Ukrinform carry on record. The dates are tentative by Zelensky's own account. Kyiv's suspicion of a phone-call ploy rests on one outlet and an anonymous official.

items.title: Russia Sends 168 More Drones at Ukraine in a Daytime Saturday Wave
items.lede: The overnight raid of 134 drones was followed by a daylight barrage, and falling debris injured a 12-year-old girl at a Kyiv mall.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 134 attack drones from 18:00 Kyiv time on Friday 30 October (17:00 CET) [11]. It said 72 of the Shahed drones were jet-powered, and Gerbera and decoy drones were also used [11]. As of 08:30 Kyiv time (07:30 CET) on Saturday, air defenses had shot down or jammed 105 drones [11][12]. Drones hit 20 locations, debris fell at 10 more, and several drones were still in the air [11]. From 06:30 to 19:30 Kyiv time on Saturday, Russia launched 168 strike drones and S8000 Banderol missiles, the Air Force said [13][14]. Air defenses shot down or jammed 122 drones and two Banderol missiles, and about 30 drones were still airborne [13][14]. In Kyiv, drone debris fell at a shopping center in the Obolonskyi district and injured a 12-year-old girl [15]. Later, a drone crashed in an open area in the Darnytskyi district, city officials said [16].

Confidence is moderate on the totals, because they are the Air Force's own preliminary figures, though at least two Ukrainian outlets carry each tally. Confidence is high on the Kyiv incidents, which city officials reported on record. No Russian Defense Ministry figure was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Oleshky Evacuees Reach Ukraine as Kyiv Declares the Mission a Success
items.lede: Zelensky said the group crossed in through the Chernihiv region and urged continued aid access to the Russian-held town, while no total headcount was released.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia have observed a ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's Kherson region, since 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October (02:00 CET) [17][18]. US First Lady Melania Trump brokered the pause [19][20], and lawmaker David Arakhamia said it runs until 22:59 Kyiv time on 1 November [21]. On Friday, Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets and Russia's ombudsman Yana Lantratova ran the joint mission [22][23][24]. Interfax, citing Russian TV channel Zvezda, said evacuees were taken to a temporary shelter in Simferopol, in occupied Crimea [25]. Lubinets had set a 14:00 local deadline for residents to leave [26][27]. On Friday evening, he reported no ceasefire violations in 87 hours [28]. On Saturday morning, Arakhamia said the final plane had landed in Gomel, Belarus [29]. By Saturday afternoon, Zelensky said the evacuees had crossed into Ukraine in the Chernihiv region [30]. He said he hopes humanitarian access to Oleshky will continue [30]. Kyrylo Budanov, head of the presidential office, said the mission succeeded and all sides kept their agreements [31].
Confidence is high that the evacuees reached Ukraine, because Zelensky and Budanov say so on record. The total headcount and the Simferopol detail from Russian state TV are not established.

items.title: Ukraine and Türkiye Agree to Work on Reviving the Black Sea Grain Corridor
items.lede: Erdoğan said Ankara will raise safe Black Sea shipping with Moscow too, calling a deal a possible boost to peace efforts after meeting Zelensky in Istanbul.

sections.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made a working visit to Istanbul on 31 October at President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's invitation, Turkish presidential communications head Burhanettin Duran had announced on X [32][33]. Duran said the talks would cover bilateral cooperation, the war between Russia and Ukraine, and the security situation in the Black Sea [32][33]. Erdoğan received him at the Dolmabahçe presidential office, and the two leaders held one-on-one talks [34][35]. Turkish Defense Minister Yaşar Güler, intelligence chief İbrahim Kalın, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, and foreign intelligence head Rustem Umierov joined the delegation talks [34]. At a news conference afterward, Zelensky said he and Erdoğan agreed to work on restoring the Black Sea grain corridor [36]. Erdoğan said Türkiye would keep talking with both sides, including Russia, to restore safe shipping in the Black Sea [37]. Erdoğan also reaffirmed Türkiye's support for Ukraine's territorial integrity [37].

Confidence is high on the leaders' statements, which they made on record at a news conference reported by Ukrainian outlets and a Turkish outlet. No Russian response to the grain corridor plan was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Fire Hits Refinery in Russia's Ufa as Airports Close Under Drone Threat
items.lede: Moscow's mayor said 11 drones were downed near the capital on Saturday, while local officials in Bashkortostan stayed silent on the blasts.

sections.text: Russia's aviation agency Rosaviatsia imposed temporary flight restrictions at Kazan and Samara airports early on Saturday 31 October, Interfax reported [38]. Restrictions followed at Yekaterinburg and Perm airports in the Urals around 04:00 CET, Interfax said [39]. Such restrictions usually accompany Ukrainian drone raids, but no drone attack on these regions was confirmed in the reports read by the cutoff. Residents of Ufa, capital of Russia's Bashkortostan region, reported explosions overnight and smoke over an industrial area on Saturday morning, BBC News Russian said, as relayed by Ukrinform [40]. Rosaviatsia closed Ufa airport around 04:00 local time (00:00 CET), and it stayed closed, the report said [40]. Astra's analysts said a key reforming unit at the Bashneft-Novoil refinery was on fire [40]. DW's Russian service, citing monitoring channels, said at least two Bashneft refineries in Ufa were burning [41]. On Saturday afternoon, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 11 drones were shot down on approach to the capital [42]. Astra reported a forest fire north of Sheremetyevo Airport near its fuel complex [42].

Confidence is moderate. The closures rest on Rosaviatsia notices relayed by Interfax. The Ufa fires rest on monitoring channels relayed by DW, BBC News Russian, and Ukrinform. No official Russian confirmation of a refinery strike was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Ukraine Says Neptune Missiles and Drones Struck a Rocket Fuel Plant in Russia
items.lede: Kyiv's General Staff reported a warehouse fire and four damaged workshops at the Rostov-region plant, which it says fuels Russian rocket launchers.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck the Kamensky Combine in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, in Russia's Rostov region, on the night of 30–31 October [43][44]. It said strike drones and the Navy's Neptune coastal missiles were used [43]. The General Staff said a warehouse of finished goods caught fire and four production workshops were damaged [43][44][41]. It said the plant makes solid rocket fuel for Uragan, Smerch, and Tornado-S rocket launchers and for other missiles [43]. Four Russian military supply depots in occupied parts of the Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Luhansk regions were also hit, it said [43]. No Russian official comment on the plant was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate. Reuters, DW, and Ukrinform each carry the General Staff claim, but the damage rests on Ukraine's own account with no independent confirmation.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Romania Scrambles F-16 Jets and Closes Iași Airspace as Two Drones Approach
items.lede: Alerts hit six counties for about two and a half hours, and the Defense Ministry said only one of the two drones was confirmed to have left.

sections.text: Romania issued air-raid alerts in six eastern counties on Saturday evening after radar tracked two drones near the border with Moldova [1][2]. Radar first detected one target about 10 kilometers from the Moldovan border, the Defense Ministry said [2]. A second target then entered Romanian airspace without authorization from the direction of Moldova [2]. The first RO-Alert went to Iași county at 16:04 CET, followed by Neamț, Vaslui, Botoșani, Bacău, and Suceava [1]. Two F-16 jets and an IAR-330 helicopter took off, and two more F-16s later joined from Fetești air base [1]. Iași airspace was closed, and a flight from Eindhoven was diverted to Suceava [1][2]. The ministry said at 18:20 CET that one of the two drones had left Romanian airspace [1]. Alerts began lifting at 18:24 CET, and Iași airspace reopened [1]. Defense Minister Radu Oprea said the priority was protecting the population and national airspace [1]. No crash, damage, or injuries were reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the alerts, the Iași closure, and the diversion, which Euronews România and RO Times reported from Romania's Defense Ministry and Agerpres. The jet count rests on Euronews România alone.

items.title: Swedish Police Board a Russia-Linked Cargo Ship Overnight Off Gotland
items.lede: Police called it a routine border check, but TV4 reported the ship's operator has been tied to suspected Russian drone operations.

sections.text: Swedish police boarded a dry-cargo ship at a port on northern Gotland overnight into Saturday [3][4]. Border police checked the crew's travel documents, a Stockholm police spokesperson said [3]. She said everything looked fine and the check found nothing to remark on [3]. She called such checks on ships routine [3]. TV4 said the ship is over 80 meters long and belongs to a company previously investigated over Russian hybrid and spying operations [4]. TV4 sources said the crew are Russian citizens and the national special forces unit took part; police declined to confirm either [4]. TV4 said ships from the same company have been linked to drone alerts in other European countries [4]. No ship name, arrest, or seizure was reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that Swedish police boarded the ship and checked crew papers, which SVT and TV4 report from a police spokesperson. The Russian crew, the special forces role, and the company's history rest on TV4's unnamed sources alone.

items.title: Drones Shut Jersey Airport to Arrivals for a Second Night
items.lede: Jersey's chief minister is seeking UK help with counter-drone technology after three more flights were canceled, while police still have no suspect.

sections.text: Unauthorized drones flew in restricted airspace near Jersey Airport on Friday evening, disrupting flights from Britain to the British Crown Dependency [5]. The first report came at about 20:20 local time (21:20 CET), and further drone activity was reported until about 22:30 (23:30 CET) [6]. Three inbound flights from London Gatwick, London Heathrow, and Southampton were diverted [5]. Jersey Police Inspector Rob McCallum said officers believed two or three drones had been in the restricted airspace [5]. He said the incident was not thought to be linked to terrorism [5]. Drones disrupted Jersey Airport again on Saturday evening [7][8]. At 21:05 CET the airport reported disruption to inbound flights from further drone activity near the airfield [7]. Three more flights into Jersey were canceled, on top of three on Friday [8]. Chief Minister Lyndon Farnham said Jersey was working with UK authorities and specialist agencies on counter-drone technology and better detection [8]. He said those responsible would face the full consequences of the law [7][8]. No operator, motive, or state link was named by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on both nights of disruption and the cancellations, which the BBC, the Jersey Evening Post, and Channel 103 reported from police and government statements. The drone count rests on one police officer's estimate.

items.title: Moldova Tracks Two Stray Drones Crossing Its Territory During Russian Strikes
items.lede: The second drone entered from Ukraine's Vinnytsia region and crossed the north in about 22 minutes, after the first had vanished from radar.

sections.text: An unauthorized drone entered Moldova's airspace on Saturday at 15:24 CET, Moldova's Air Operations Center said [9][10]. It came from the direction of Semionovca in Ukraine's Odesa region and headed toward Plopi in the Transnistrian region [9][10]. Moldova restricted airspace in the north at 15:46 CET and in the center at 15:52 CET [10]. The drone disappeared from radar near Țibirica in Călărași district at 15:54 CET [9][10]. Authorities reopened northern and central airspace at 16:14 CET after the drone left Moldovan airspace [9]. The Defense Ministry linked the incident to massive Russian attacks on Ukraine [9]. A second drone entered Moldova's airspace at 16:50 CET from the direction of Ukraine's Vinnytsia region, the Defense Ministry said [11]. It flew past Dondușeni and over three villages in Edineț district in northern Moldova [11]. The ministry said it left Moldovan airspace near Viișoara at 17:12 CET [11]. No damage, injuries, or drone type had been reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on both flight paths and the airspace closures, which Moldova's Defense Ministry published and MOLDPRES and TVR Moldova reported. The drones' type and origin were not officially named.

items.title: Moldova Restores 61 Online Public Services After Its Record Data Breach
items.lede: Moldova will accept only physical IDs in Sunday's local elections after the breach, while 21 e-government services stay offline and intrusion attempts continue.

sections.text: Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency said Friday that 61 digital public services were back on the EVO portal, while 21 stay offline until security checks end [12]. The agency said attackers were still trying to break into government systems, but checks found no new data theft and no changes to state registers [12]. The 19 to 23 October attack extracted personal data of more than 750,000 citizens, and the Chișinău Municipal Prosecutor's Office has opened a criminal case [12][13]. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Vasile Tofan said authorities were examining possible foreign state involvement. A government spokesperson said the incident could be part of a broader hybrid campaign [13]. Moldova has not attributed the attack to any country or group [13]. Later Friday, the agency made an EVO app update mandatory to add security measures [14]. On Saturday, the Central Electoral Commission said voters in the seven localities holding new local elections and a local referendum on Sunday must show physical IDs and cannot use EVO digital documents [15]. It also suspended online filing of electoral complaints after the cyber incidents [16].

Confidence is high on the restoration figures, app update, election rules, and breach figures, reported by state agency Moldpres and, for the breach, The Record. Foreign state involvement is unconfirmed.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: EU's Kallas Warns Putin's G20 Return Would Normalize War Crimes
items.lede: The EU foreign policy chief spoke after European officials refused to pose beside Russia's Sergei Lavrov at a G20 meeting in Atlanta.

sections.text: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Saturday that Russian President Vladimir Putin's possible return to the G20 risks normalizing Russia's war crimes in Ukraine [1]. She spoke in a Bloomberg TV interview, Politico Europe reported [1]. The United States hosts the G20 leaders' summit in Florida in December, and Putin has not said whether he will attend [1]. At a G20 ministers' meeting in Atlanta, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio canceled the family photo after European officials refused to stand beside Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov [1]. Kallas called the U.S. sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine very positive and urged tougher sanctions on Russia [1]. She also rejected reported Pentagon calls for NATO states to soften their criticism of the Kremlin [1].

Confidence is moderate. Politico Europe reported the remarks from a Bloomberg TV interview; the Bloomberg video was not checked. The EEAS press page showed her G20 remarks but no transcript of this interview.

items.title: Poland's Tusk Vows No Compromise on Constitutional Court Overhaul
items.lede: The prime minister spoke on television after riot police guarded the court, whose sidelined leadership calls the move a coup, and President Karol Nawrocki called party talks.

sections.text: Riot police deployed on Friday evening at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw after Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska suspended its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and vice-president, Bartłomiej Sochański, for one month. Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek has asked for both judges' immunity to be lifted so they can be charged for keeping parliament-elected judges off the bench [2][3]. The court wrote on X that everyone taking part was committing the crime of a coup d'état, as Law and Justice supporters, joined by leader Jarosław Kaczyński, protested outside [2][4]. Nawrocki canceled his Senegal trip in mid-flight and went to the court at about 01:00, where video showed scuffles with judges at the entrance [2][3]. Korwin-Piotrowska has called the court's general assembly for 3 November [3]. On Saturday morning, Nawrocki's chief of staff said the president would hold urgent consultations with government and opposition parties [5]. In a prime-time TV address on Saturday night, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk vowed to see the court overhaul through, saying some matters allow no compromise [6].

Confidence is high on the suspension, the police deployment, the court's statement, and Tusk's address, reported by the BBC, El País, ANSA, and the Guardian. No ruling on the suspension's legality was found by the cutoff.

items.title: France Arrests 565 as Cost-of-Living Marches End in Paris Clashes
items.lede: The Interior Ministry counted 320,000 marchers nationwide, and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called a firebomb attack on a gendarme attempted murder.

sections.text: France's third Saturday of cost-of-living protests drew 320,000 people nationwide, including 70,000 in Paris, the Interior Ministry and Paris police said [7][8]. Student and high school unions counted nearly 500,000 [7]. The Interior Ministry said police had arrested 565 people nationwide by 21:00 [8][9]. The Paris march kept to the outer boulevards after France's Conseil d'État canceled the Bastille–Nation route [7][10]. At the dispersal, police used tear gas and baton charges against groups throwing paving stones and a firebomb [7][9]. By 21:00, Paris police reported 79 arrests and five officers hurt, three of them burned by a firebomb [8]. The Interior Ministry said the IGPN and IGGN police watchdogs had 83 cases from the school protests, including a Reims marcher's shin seriously injured by a police grenade, franceinfo reported [11][12]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called the firebombing of a gendarme attempted murder [7][9]. The prefecture's order n° 2026-01485 bars everyone from the Place de la République and Châtelet-Les Halles sectors from 23:00 to 06:00 on Saturday and Sunday nights [13][14]. A planned 0.8% riot insurance surcharge from 2027 still needs Conseil d'État validation [15].

Confidence is high on turnout, arrests, and the Paris clashes, which franceinfo, the Guardian, and RTBF with AFP attribute to the Interior Ministry and Paris police. No overnight Halloween toll was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Spain's Renfe Orders Drivers to Slow Trains After Deadly Urda Crash
items.lede: An Adif incident log shows the LZB signaling system failed 23 minutes before Wednesday's collision, which killed 69 people on the Madrid–Seville high-speed line.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Spain's state rail operator Renfe will order its more than 6,000 drivers to slow down sharply whenever the LZB train-protection system fails, El País reported [16]. A draft order caps speed at 40 km/h in such cases, and the paper said it could still change [16]. Renfe is drafting the final version with infrastructure manager Adif [16]. The crash near Urda, in Toledo province, killed 69 people on Wednesday, 28 October [16]. A Renfe AVE train hit a stationary Iryo train [17]. An Adif incident log opened at 08:30, 23 minutes before the crash, recorded a failure of the LZB control center at Urda [17]. It also noted power losses, downed phone lines, and intermittent data loss, El País reported [17]. The paper said drivers then received disjointed instructions from the Madrid-Atocha control center [17].
Confidence is moderate. Both reports come from El País, which cites Adif's incident log and a Renfe draft order it obtained. Neither Renfe nor Adif had publicly confirmed the order by the cutoff.

items.title: Dutch Police Arrest 34, Mostly Teens, in The Hague Over Gen Z Protest Calls
items.lede: Police said no major incidents occurred, though fireworks thrown at officers sent one to the hospital with possible hearing damage.

sections.text: Dutch riot police briefly cleared the Korte Voorhout in The Hague at about 15:15 on Saturday after youths ignored orders to move to the Malieveld, Omroep West reported [18]. Calls for a 'Gen Z protest' had spread on social media during the week, and shops in The Hague, Maastricht, and Amsterdam were boarded up [19]. The city had banned face coverings for Saturday [19]. Police also arrested several protesters in Delft [19]. Several hundred people, including ADO Den Haag soccer fans, gathered on the Plein and said they had come to protect the city [18]. The city extended an emergency order to the Malieveld and the central station area in the afternoon [18]. Maastricht police reported no incidents, and Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Utrecht stayed quiet [19]. By evening, Dutch police said they had arrested 34 people in The Hague, mostly minors aged 15 to 18 from across the Netherlands [20]. One officer went to the hospital with possible hearing damage after illegal fireworks were thrown at police [20]. Mayor Jan van Zanen said heavy policing kept the situation under control [20].
Confidence is high on the arrests, the injury, and the emergency order, reported by NOS, Omroep West, and NU.nl and attributed to Dutch police and the mayor.

items.title: Spanish Police Check 1,000 Youths as Barcelona Blocus Calls Fizzle
items.lede: A heavy Catalan police presence met the Blocus looting calls, a week after 133 arrests downtown, and several stores closed early.

sections.text: Spain's Catalan police and Barcelona city police flooded downtown Barcelona on Saturday afternoon for the Blocus calls, El País reported [21]. Officers carried out about 1,000 ID checks and searched some bags, and the afternoon passed without major incidents [21]. Police took 12 minors carrying items such as balaclavas to a station for their protection until parents collected them [21]. Many shops boarded up windows, and some closed early [21]. Catalan police had set their top risk level, level 4, for only the second time for a protest since 2019 [22][23]. A court in Torrent on Saturday ordered the alleged Spanish founder of Blocus jailed after his Friday arrest in Valencia province [22]. Spanish police had arrested 10 young people nationwide for urging looting [23]. Police also had four Telegram channels shut down, and El País said Catalan police saw little activity in the groups [22][21]. The 24 October Barcelona looting ended with 133 arrests, 89 of them minors [21].

Confidence is high on the deployment and the quiet evening, reported by El País and consistent with RTVE and La Vanguardia. No official Catalan police tally or late-night update was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Italian Police Charge Students and Fire a Water Cannon in Turin During General Strike
items.lede: Police later searched 60 people who had urged violence online, after unions claimed more than 1 million marchers and the interior ministry counted 255,000.

sections.text: Students and workers marched Friday in Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna, and Naples during Italy's general strike over living costs and school funding, RTBF reported, citing AFP [24]. In Turin's Piazza Castello, police made two brief charges and used a water cannon when marchers behind shields reached the cordon protecting the prefecture. Protesters threw red-paint eggs and bottles, ANSA reported [25]. Two people were held, one of them bruised [25]. In the evening, protesters threw bottles at police in Rome and Turin, and police charged and used water cannon. USB claimed more than 1 million marchers nationwide, while the interior ministry counted 255,000 [26]. Interior Minister Piantedosi said the right to protest had been "guaranteed despite some violent people" [26]. Unions demand restored wage indexation and lower VAT on essentials, and have called another general strike for 20 November [24]. On Saturday, Italian police said they carried out 60 searches in 23 cities targeting people who urged violence at recent protests in chats and on social media [27].

Confidence is high on the strike and the Rome and Turin clashes, reported by RTBF with AFP and ANSA. Crowd figures are contested. Turin police later put the day's tally at 12 people reported to prosecutors and 256 identified [28].

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Lithuania's Cities Have Evacuation Routes but Lack Buses for Disabled Residents
items.lede: Only about 800 of more than 6,500 public shelters are adapted for people with disabilities, and 13 municipalities have none at all.

sections.text: Kaunas, Šiauliai, Panevėžys, and Marijampolė told the Elta news agency they have evacuation routes, assembly points, and vehicles planned, LRT reported [1]. Lithuania's national plan assumes about 75% of residents could leave on their own and 25% would need organized transport [1]. The plan requires evacuation within 72 hours of an official decision [1]. Kaunas and Marijampolė said their adapted vehicles would not carry all residents with disabilities at once [1]. Šiauliai said its fleet could move about 6,000 people in one trip [1]. In a separate LRT report, disability groups said shelter access is their biggest worry [2]. Data from the LT72 preparedness site show just over 800 of more than 6,500 shelters, about 12%, are adapted for people with disabilities, and 13 municipalities have none [2].
Confidence is moderate: the facts rest on two LRT reports, one relaying an Elta survey of city halls; the national plan and LT72 data were not read directly.

items.title: Lithuanian Prosecutors Press On With Army Contract Probe Into Kaunas Firm Taiklu
items.lede: Separately, the procurement watchdog found three kinds of violations in the army's purchase of mobile dragon's teeth barriers, and lawmakers voted to send that case to prosecutors.

sections.text: Lithuania's Prosecutor General's Office said a criminal probe into army contracts won by the Kaunas company Taiklu is still under way, BNS reported via LRT [3]. Military police opened the case in March last year over stump-milling work at the Rūdninkai training ground [3]. Prosecutors said the probe covers suspected document forgery and failure to perform official duties [3]. It now also covers Taiklu's demining contract at the same range, spokeswoman Rita Stundienė said [3]. The Public Procurement Office told the Seimas audit committee this week that army logistics leaders committed three categories of violations on a dragon's teeth barrier tender [3]. The committee voted to refer the case to prosecutors [3]. Deputy Defense Minister Gabrielius Gorbačevskis said the army opened an internal review but the state suffered no financial loss [3]. Taiklu has said ground conditions kept it from milling deeper [3].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one BNS report carried by LRT quoting on-record officials; the prosecutors' and procurement office's own statements were not read.

items.title: Estonia's President Picks Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask as Chancellor of Justice
items.lede: Kask pledged to keep the ombudsman office out of politics, while Isamaa, EKRE, and the Social Democrats set out their own tests before a vote.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Estonian President Ülle Madise proposed to parliament on Saturday that Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask become the next chancellor of justice, ERR reported [4]. Madise held the post until she took office as president earlier in October [4]. She called Kask a highly regarded expert on constitutional law and fundamental rights [4]. Kask was a Tallinn Circuit Court judge from 2004 to 2024 and joined the Supreme Court in September 2024 [4]. Parliament appoints the chancellor for seven years, and its party groups plan to meet Kask the week after next [5]. Kask told ERR the office must not be political and that political questions belong to parliament and the government [5]. He said he would focus first on social rights for people who struggle to defend themselves in court [5]. Isamaa named the Estonian language and a 2,000-person waiting list for special care as its questions [5]. The Social Democrats want the chancellor to keep working on personal data protection [5]. EKRE said Kask must prove his independence and defend e-voting oversight [5]. No vote date was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on two ERR reports quoting the president, the nominee, and party figures; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Estonia's Michal Vows Not to Go Quiet on Russia Despite Reported US Pressure
items.lede: A former diplomat who recently joined the opposition Isamaa party said Tallinn's predictable message risks costing it invitations to key talks, opening a domestic debate over tone.

sections.text: Citing four anonymous sources, Reuters reported Friday that Pentagon officials urged Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia to tone down public talk of the Russian threat, LRT and BNS summarized [6]. Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said the United States had made no official proposal [7]. Foreign Ministry Secretary General Jonatan Vseviov said he knew of no official request [8]. Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said he had no information about such appeals [6]. A top Lithuanian presidential adviser, Deividas Matulionis, said Lithuania should not deliberately provoke Russia [9]. In a longer ERR interview published Saturday, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said no such request had reached him [10][11]. He said Russia is killing women and children and that pleasing dictators or staying silent is no solution [10]. Former diplomat Jaap Ora, who recently joined the opposition Isamaa party, said Estonia's foreign policy message has become predictable [12]. Ora wrote on social media that public messages must be carefully calibrated or allies may stop inviting Estonia to key talks [12]. The Reuters original was not read.
Confidence is high on the on-record Estonian and Lithuanian statements; confidence is moderate on the US appeals themselves, which rest on anonymous sources relayed from Reuters.

items.title: Estonia's Enefit Power Will Burn Shale Oil to Heat Narva From Sunday
items.lede: The state-owned firm cites high gas prices, low EU storage, and Middle East supply risks, using an exemption the environment board granted on 21 October.

sections.text: Enefit Power, part of Estonia's state-owned Eesti Energia, will start burning shale oil in the reserve boiler house of the Balti power plant on Sunday, ERR reported [13]. The switch applies when the plant's unit 11 is uncompetitive on the power market or out of service [13]. Board chairman Raine Pajo told the environment board and Climate Minister Erkki Keldo the conditions for the exemption had been met [13]. He cited price swings, rising winter demand, below-normal EU gas storage, and the risk of new gas supply disruptions under the environment board's 21 October order [13]. Pajo said the Middle East crisis pushed European gas prices to a four-year high in October [13]. He said the step is temporary and aims to keep district heating affordable for Narva residents [13].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one ERR report quoting the company's letter; no environment board response was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Latvia Bars Russian TV Host Ksenia Sobchak From Entering the Country
items.lede: Foreign Minister Baiba Braže also added Sobchak's husband, theater director Konstantin Bogomolov, to the indefinite entry ban list.

sections.text: Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braže put Russian television and internet host Ksenia Sobchak on Latvia's list of unwanted persons, LSM reported Saturday [14]. Braže announced the decision on X under the Immigration Law, which lets the foreign minister decide such listings [14]. Sobchak is barred from entering Latvia indefinitely [14]. The list also now includes theater director Konstantin Bogomolov, whom LSM describes as Sobchak's husband and who once staged plays in Liepāja [14]. LSM said Latvian foreign ministers have regularly banned entertainment figures who backed the policies of aggressor states [14]. No reason specific to Sobchak was found in the report.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LSM report relaying the minister's post; the post itself was not read.

items.title: Belgrade Prosecutors Find Only Copies in Sacks Dumped Outside a Serbian Town Hall
items.lede: Prosecutors see no grounds for a criminal case so far after residents reported shredded files outside the municipal offices of Zemun, a Belgrade district.

sections.text: Serbian prosecutors said 10 sacks of destroyed papers dumped outside Belgrade's Zemun municipality on 30 October held only discarded copies, Vijesti reported, citing Beta and Insajder [1]. The Third Basic Public Prosecutor's Office said the originals remain in the municipal offices [1]. A prosecutor and Zemun police went to the scene after residents complained [1]. They checked all 10 sacks and security camera footage [1]. They interviewed 21 people, including the municipality's president and its head of public procurement [1]. Prosecutors said they will act if new evidence emerges [1].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the prosecutors' statement as relayed by Beta and Insajder through Vijesti; the statement itself was not read.

items.title: Kosovo's Kurti Urges Serbia's Incoming Government to Accept Kosovo's Independence
items.lede: The Student List, which ended Vučić's 14-year rule, says it will keep the EU-led dialogue but has called Kosovo part of Serbia.

sections.text: Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti said on Saturday he hopes Serbia's new government will change its approach to Kosovo as an independent state, RFE/RL reported [2]. He spoke at a rally of his Self-Determination party [2]. Kurti said a new approach should also cover ethnic Albanians in Preševo, Bujanovac, and Medveđa [2]. He called for mutual recognition and full normalization [2]. He did not address resuming the stalled Brussels dialogue [2]. The Student List won 52.54% of the vote on 25 October, ending Vučić's 14-year rule [2]. It says it will continue the EU-mediated dialogue, though its stated position is that Kosovo is an integral part of Serbia [2]. Its lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, told RFE/RL that the new government would honor international agreements signed under Vučić [2].
Confidence is high on Kurti's remarks, reported by RFE/RL from a public rally; no Student List response was found by the cutoff.

items.title: EU Draft Report Faults Serbia's Former Government on Media Freedom and Courts
items.lede: The European Commission publishes the assessment on 4 November, but it covers only the period before the student movement won power on 25 October.

sections.text: Serbia slid further on media freedom and made no progress on the judiciary and fundamental rights, according to the European Commission's annual report seen by RFE/RL [3]. The report finds limited progress against corruption and organized crime [3]. It rates Serbia's alignment with EU foreign and security policy as low [3]. It lists Serbia with Bosnia, Georgia, and Turkey as countries where the risk of "state capture" remains [3]. It says police often failed to act on attacks against students, activists, and peaceful protesters [3]. It says high officials' support for Ratko Mladić's funeral glorifies war crimes and undermines Serbia's EU path [3]. The Commission publishes the report on 4 November, and its reporting period ends in September 2026, before the student movement won power [3].
Confidence is moderate: the contents rest on RFE/RL's account of an unpublished draft; the Commission has not released the text.

items.title: Albanian Police Fire Tear Gas as Tirana Protesters Throw Molotov Cocktails
items.lede: Police arrested three people after the 19th day of protests, as students kept opposition lawmakers at a distance from their rally.

sections.text: Protesters in Albania's capital, Tirana, threw volleys of Molotov cocktails at police on Saturday, Gazeta Express reported, citing Top Channel [4]. Police answered with tear gas and water cannon to disperse the crowd, and the area stayed tense [4] [5]. At a student protest outside the Education Ministry, the arrival of Democratic Party supporters and lawmakers set off a brief fight between two people, Kosovo Online reported, citing Koha [5]. Students said they wanted their movement to stay independent of parties [5]. They chanted "We are the opposition!" and "Rama to prison, Berisha to prison" [5]. Top Channel reported that three people were arrested and that police seized Molotov cocktails, Kosovo Online said [6]. Police said a masked group threw the stones and had been identified [6]. Clashes moved to the government building at about 16:30 and spread into nearby streets [6]. Prime Minister Edi Rama mocked the protesters on social media [6]. Democratic Party leader Sali Berisha did not join the march [6]. No police injury figures were found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the clashes, reported by Gazeta Express and Kosovo Online from Albanian broadcasters; the arrest count rests on Top Channel, and no full police statement was read.

items.title: Serbia's Central Bank Revokes Alta Bank's License Overnight
items.lede: The regulator also filed a criminal complaint against the lender and its officials, and insured deposits are due within seven working days.

sections.text: The National Bank of Serbia revoked Alta Bank's operating license in a statement sent to the media at 02:25 CET on Saturday, Danas reported [7]. The central bank said the bank's financial condition had worsened significantly and depositors' interests were at risk [7]. The Deposit Insurance Agency will be named receiver and will pay insured amounts within seven working days [7]. Four vice governors said they learned of the bank's true condition only at an emergency board session on Friday evening, N1 reported [8]. They said it differed sharply from the reports the bank had filed [8]. The organized crime prosecutor's office said it received a criminal complaint from the central bank against Alta Bank and several officials [8]. It said it had asked the central bank on 27 October for data on the bank's foreign transfers [8]. N1 filmed police with rifles and many police vehicles outside the bank's New Belgrade headquarters [8]. Deposit Insurance Agency director Ljubica Pantelić told Radio Belgrade on Saturday that the Belgrade Commercial Court should formally open bankruptcy proceedings on Monday [9][10].
Confidence is high on the license revocation and payout terms, from the central bank statement reported by Danas and N1; the central bank's own page could not be opened.

items.title: Thieves Take More Than 100 Firearms From a Warehouse in Kosovo's Gjakova
items.lede: Police have opened an investigation but have not said who owns the depot, what type of weapons are missing, or who is behind it.

sections.text: Kosovo Police said in their daily report that more than 100 firearms were stolen from a warehouse in Gjakova, N1 reported, citing KoSSev [11]. Two men reported the theft to police at about 18:00 on Friday, 30 October [11]. Police units went to the scene, the prosecutor was informed, and an investigation began [11]. The report did not name the warehouse owner or the type of weapons [11]. It also did not say how the weapons went missing [11].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the police report as relayed by KoSSev and N1; the police report itself was not read.

items.title: Italy's Defense Minister Visits Survivors of the EUFOR Chinook Crash in Bosnia
items.lede: The crash, which killed four of the 15 EUFOR personnel aboard, is the most serious air accident for international forces in Bosnia since 1997 by total casualties, Klix.ba says.

sections.text: Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto and Chief of Defense Gen. Luciano Portolano flew to Bosnia and Herzegovina with an Italian medical team, according to a EUFOR text published by Sarajevo Times [12]. They visited injured personnel at hospitals in Brčko and Tuzla [12]. EUFOR commander Maj. Gen. Maurizio Fronda and Bosnian Defense Minister Zukan Helez met them at Tuzla airport [12]. The Italian CH-47 Chinook crashed near Brčko on Thursday, killing four people and injuring 11 [12]. Sarajevo Times, citing Klix.ba, said it is the deadliest air accident for international forces in Bosnia by total casualties since a 1997 UN helicopter crash [13]. No cause had been published by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the visit and toll, from EUFOR's own text; the historical comparison rests on Klix.ba via Sarajevo Times.

items.title: Georgians March in Tbilisi on the 703rd Day of Pro-EU Protests
items.lede: Relatives of jailed demonstrators joined the rally and aimed its main slogan at Bidzina Ivanishvili, the billionaire founder of the ruling Georgian Dream party.

sections.text: Protesters in Georgia held their weekly Saturday march in the capital, Tbilisi, on 31 October, JAMnews reported [1]. It marked 703 days of continuous pro-European protests [1]. The main slogan was "Georgia against Ivanishvili" [1]. Family members of activists detained at earlier rallies joined the march [1]. Protesters demand early elections, the release of political prisoners, and repeal of laws passed by Georgian Dream [1]. JAMnews counts about 150 prisoners of conscience in Georgia [1]. No arrests or clashes were reported by the cutoff, and no turnout figure was found.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on JAMnews photo coverage; no police statement or second outlet was read.

items.title: Azerbaijani Media Accuse Turkish Outlets of Passing Off an Old Aliyev Speech
items.lede: Baku-based outlets say Turkish papers presented a 2020 victory address as a new warning to Ankara, feeding talk of a rift between the allies.

sections.text: Azerbaijan's Report.az and Oxu.Az accused some Turkish media of spreading a misleading video of President Ilham Aliyev [2]. An unofficial TikTok account posted footage of Aliyev with audio from his 10 November 2020 address on the Karabakh war [2]. Turkish papers Milli Gazete and Sonsöz presented it as a post from Aliyev's official account [2]. Social media users then asked whether it was a message to Turkey [2]. Oxu.Az said Aliyev has no official TikTok account [2]. It urged the outlets to correct their reports [2]. No Turkish response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the dispute, which rests on Report.az relaying Oxu.Az; the Turkish reports were not read.

items.title: Armenia's Foreign Minister Discusses Peace With Azerbaijan at Gulf Talks in Bahrain
items.lede: Ararat Mirzoyan met the Gulf Cooperation Council's chief in Manama and raised the US-backed TRIPP transit route.

sections.text: Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan met Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary-General Jasem Albudaiwi in Manama, Bahrain, Report.az reported [3]. Mirzoyan posted about the meeting on X on 31 October [3]. He said they discussed closer institutional cooperation and economic ties [3]. They also discussed regional transport links and the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity project [3]. They discussed further institutionalizing peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan and the situation in the Middle East [3].
Confidence is high, as Report.az quotes the minister's own post; no GCC readout was read.

items.title: Armenia Starts Issuing Biometric Passports, With Pashinyan the First Applicant
items.lede: A private partner, HayPass, runs the new centers; officials promise 23 offices nationwide by early 2027 and documents within 14 working days.

sections.text: Armenia launched a new biometric passport and ID card system on Saturday, Armenpress reported [4]. Private company HayPass opened its first service center at a Yerevan mall [4]. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan was the first visitor and gave his own biometric data [4]. Interior Minister Arpine Sargsyan said the system would end identity theft [4]. She said the partnership compressed seven to eight years of work into about a year [4]. Applicants must pre-register online, and a passport costs 28,650 drams [4]. Twelve regional offices open on Monday, with 23 planned by the first quarter of 2027 [4].
Confidence is moderate: the details rest on Armenpress, the state news agency, which reported from the opening; no second outlet was read.

items.title: Azerbaijan Welcomes Turkey's Nominee for UN Secretary-General
items.lede: Baku's warm words for OSCE chief Sinirlioğlu come after Aliyev skipped Friday's Turkic summit in Ankara amid strained ties.

sections.text: Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry welcomed Turkey's nomination of Feridun Sinirlioğlu, now secretary general of the OSCE, as UN secretary-general, APA and Trend reported [5] [6]. Spokesperson Aykhan Hajizada spoke Saturday in response to a reporter's question [5]. He said the choice should rest on candidates' qualifications, diplomatic experience, impartiality, and ability to build consensus [5] [6]. He said consultations among member states should produce a decision that makes the UN more effective [6]. Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev skipped the Organization of Turkic States summit in Ankara on Friday amid strained ties, as reported in earlier editions. No Turkish reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the statement, carried by APA and Trend from the Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry; the link to the summit row is context, not stated by Baku.

items.title: UN Biodiversity Talks Hosted by Armenia End With the 'Yerevan Pathway'
items.lede: Delegates negotiated for about 12 hours from Friday night into Saturday morning to adopt roughly 50 decisions, though splits over nature finance persisted.

sections.text: More than 100 countries reached a deal at the COP17 UN biodiversity conference in Armenia's capital, Yerevan, Xinhua reported [7]. The final session ran about 12 hours, from Friday night into Saturday morning [7]. Delegates adopted the Yerevan Pathway to speed up action toward the 2030 nature targets [7]. It calls for stronger national plans, better monitoring, and more financing [7]. Divisions over finance, harmful subsidies, and scientific evidence remained [7]. Armenian Environment Minister Hambardzum Matevosyan, the conference president, said about 50 decisions were adopted [8] [7]. Parties chose Quito, Ecuador, to host COP18 in 2028 [7].
Confidence is high, from Xinhua's on-site report and Armenpress coverage of the president's news conference; the convention secretariat's own text was not read.

items.title: Fitch Lifts Georgia's Credit Outlook to Positive but Keeps the BB Rating
items.lede: The agency credits fast-growing foreign reserves, a low current account deficit, and growth that averaged above 8% from 2023 to 2025.

sections.text: Fitch Ratings kept Georgia's sovereign credit rating at BB on 30 October and changed the outlook from stable to positive, RFE/RL's Georgian service reported, citing the Finance Ministry [9]. The rating has not changed in three years [9]. Fitch cited rapid reserve growth, a low current account deficit, and high growth, which averaged above 8% from 2023 to 2025 [9]. It also cited prudent fiscal policy, moderate government debt, and a stable banking system [9]. Fitch said Georgia keeps growing strongly despite higher geopolitical risks and energy prices [9]. Fitch's own release was not read by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on RFE/RL's Georgian service relaying the Finance Ministry; a Trend report was paywalled.

items.title: Berlin's Left Party Votes to Open Coalition Talks With Greens and SPD
items.lede: Negotiations on a Left-led government for Germany's capital start Monday, and party leader Elif Eralp accused Chancellor Merz of pressuring her partners.

sections.text: The Left Party in Berlin, Germany's capital, voted at a state party congress Saturday to open coalition talks with the Greens and the SPD [1] [2]. A clear majority of delegates backed the move [1] [2]. The Greens and the SPD had already agreed to talks [1] [2]. Negotiations are set to begin Monday, six weeks after the Berlin election [1]. The planned Left-led alliance has drawn controversy across Germany for weeks [1]. Left parliamentary leader Elif Eralp told delegates she will not give up her bid to become Berlin's governing mayor [1]. She accused Chancellor Friedrich Merz of trying to blackmail the Greens and the SPD into blocking the coalition [1].
Confidence is high. tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk both report the vote. No response from Merz to Eralp's accusation was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Islamist Antisemitic Crimes in Germany Reach a Record 670 Cases in 2025
items.lede: The total rose about 6% from 2024, according to a federal analysis requested by a Green lawmaker, and Jewish leaders called the level unbearable.

sections.text: Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office recorded 670 Islamist-motivated antisemitic crimes in 2025, a new high, Welt am Sonntag reported [3] [4]. That is about 6% more than the 631 cases recorded in 2024 [3]. The newspaper cited a special federal government analysis prepared for Green lawmaker Lamya Kaddor [3]. The crimes range from glorifying terrorism and insults to property damage and serious violence [3]. The numbers have risen sharply since the Hamas attack on Israel in 2023 [3]. The Central Council of Jews in Germany warned of an unbearable level, and ministers called for tougher action [3].

Confidence is moderate. The figures come from one newspaper report on a government analysis, relayed by Stuttgarter Zeitung and Deutschlandfunk. The BKA had not published the numbers itself by the cutoff.

items.title: Rioters Loot Frankfurt Shops After Germany's Mostly Peaceful Gen Z Rallies
items.lede: Hesse's interior minister blamed about 100 left-wing extremists, Berlin police reported 27 officers hurt, and organizers set a new protest date of 20 November.

sections.text: Germany's 'Gen Z regelt' youth rallies drew tens of thousands of people in more than 30 cities on Saturday and stayed mostly peaceful during the day [5] [6]. Reporters in many cities put turnout at about half of what organizers had expected [6] [7]. Berlin police counted up to 5,000 people at the Brandenburg Gate [8] [9]. Stuttgart police stopped the march several times over masks and pyrotechnics [10] [11]. Violence broke out in several cities after the rallies ended [8] [12]. In Frankfurt, masked rioters smashed shop windows, looted stores, and attacked a gun shop [8]. Police seized two weapons taken from the shop and reported numerous arrests [8]. Several officers were hurt by thrown objects [8] [5]. Hesse Interior Minister Roman Poseck blamed about 100 violent left-wing extremists [8]. In Berlin, 27 officers suffered minor injuries at a separate march that began at Rosenthaler Platz [8] [5]. Hamburg saw burning barricades, and police used water cannons [12] [5]. Cologne police tied riots near the cathedral more to Halloween than to the protests [6] [8]. The organizers plan to join Europe-wide youth protests on 20 November [6] [5].

Confidence is high on the riots, injuries, and police statements, reported by tagesschau, dpa, and Deutschlandfunk. No nationwide arrest count was available by the cutoff, and the Frankfurt looters have not been identified.

items.title: Warning Strikes Begin at Midnight in Germany's Metal Industry Pay Dispute
items.lede: About 300 night-shift workers walked out at a tinplate plant in Andernach, and the union plans to widen the action nationwide in the coming days.

sections.text: Germany's IG Metall union began warning strikes in the metal and electrical industry just after midnight, when a no-strike obligation expired [13] [14]. About 300 night-shift workers at thyssenkrupp Rasselstein in Andernach, Rhineland-Palatinate, stopped work and rallied at the plant gate [13] [14]. A walkout also began at RF360 Europe/Qualcomm, a mobile-phone parts supplier in Munich [14]. Regional union leader Joerg Koehlinger called the Andernach walkout the start of a massive strike phase [13]. The union said the strikes will spread across Germany in the coming days [15] [14]. The union had said a large Bavarian carmaker will be hit for the first time on Monday [16]. IG Metall wants a 5% raise over 12 months and job guarantees for about 3.7 million workers [14] [15]. Employers have offered a one-time payment next year and a 1.3% raise in 2028 [15] [13].
Confidence is high on the start of the strikes, reported by SWR, BR24, and Deutschlandfunk from union statements. Turnout figures beyond Andernach were not available by the cutoff.

items.title: German Police Examine Left-Wing Claim Over Arson at Rheinmetall Drone Site
items.lede: A posting on a platform that intelligence officials rate as extremist claims responsibility for Friday's fire at the Hesse construction site, and police say they are examining it closely.

sections.text: German police said Saturday they are examining a claim of responsibility for Friday's arson at a construction site near Kassel, where Rheinmetall plans a drone center [17]. The claim appeared on an online platform that Germany's domestic intelligence agency classifies as left-wing extremist [17]. Three construction machines burned at the former Kassel-Calden airfield early Friday, and police believe the fire was set on purpose [17]. The police unit for politically motivated crime is investigating a suspected political motive [17]. Hesse Interior Minister Roman Poseck called the fire a "targeted attack" and said it showed the left-wing extremist scene has radicalized [17]. Police are still seeking witnesses and have not given a damage estimate [17]. Rheinmetall is investing more than 260 million euros in Kassel and Calden for logistics and drone testing, and the state of Hesse is adding 25 million euros [17].
Confidence is moderate. Police confirm the claim exists but have not judged whether it is authentic. The account rests on hessenschau, with the same dpa report carried by other outlets.

items.title: Germany's Merz Agrees Closer Defense Ties With South Korea on Asia Trip
items.lede: The chancellor said he will count on Asian partners' support when the coalition backing Ukraine meets in Berlin in November.

sections.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz ended a five-day trip to Singapore, Japan, and South Korea on Saturday [18] [19]. He stressed the importance of trade with all three countries [19] [18]. Merz agreed with South Korea to expand defense cooperation, including on cybersecurity [18]. He said Germany wants to build a network of mid-sized partners to balance major powers such as China and the United States [18]. North Korean soldiers fighting for Russia in Ukraine came up in his talks in all three capitals [18]. Merz said he would count on their support in the coalition of the willing, which he has invited to meet in Berlin in November [18]. He also visited Panmunjom on the border between the two Koreas [18].
Confidence is moderate. The defense and Ukraine details rest on one tagesschau report from the traveling press. Deutschlandfunk confirms only that the trip ended with a focus on trade.
